source_row.rationale: Guideline-directed beta-blockers are foundational therapy for HFrEF. In hospitalized patients, initiation is appropriate after clinical stabilization and before discharge when feasible. Existing beta-blocker therapy is generally continued unless clinical circumstances such as marked volume overload, marginal low output, or other intolerance require adjustment. The prior wording incorrectly implied that beta-blockers are broadly avoided throughout acute decompensation.
source_row.source_detail: Hospitalized HFrEF guidance: initiate guideline-directed therapy after clinical stability is achieved; beta-blocker initiation before discharge is reasonable once stabilized, while dose reduction/withholding may be considered with marked volume overload or marginal low output.
source_row.source_name: AHA/ACC/HFSA — 2022 Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
source_row.stem: A client hospitalized with acute decompensated HFrEF is being considered for initiation of an evidence-based beta-blocker. When is initiation most appropriate?
